 "density": "num_edges / (n*(n-1)). A value above ~0.01 means neighbourhoods cover a large share of the graph.",

 "max_degree": "Largest neighbour count.",
 "degree_std": "Standard deviation of the degree.",
 "clustering_coeff": "Average local clustering coefficient (triangle closure). Estimated by sampling above 2M edges.",
 "num_communities": "Number of communities found by Louvain. Louvain is run WITHOUT a fixed seed, so this and the two fields below vary slightly between runs.",
 "modularity": "Modularity of that Louvain partition. Below ~0.3 the partition is weak, so community-relative views have little to measure against.",

 "feature_sparsity": "Fraction of attribute entries that are exactly zero.",

You do not know how the graph was built or what its anomalies look like; reason only from the evidence given. Select the small set of paradigms (1 to 4) whose assumptions the evidence supports, favouring complementary views over redundant ones. Reply with JSON only.

 "num_nodes": "Number of nodes.",
 "num_edges": "Number of directed edge entries in the edge list (each undirected edge appears twice).",
 "density": "num_edges / (n*(n-1)). A value above ~0.01 means neighbourhoods cover a large share of the graph.",
 "avg_degree": "Mean number of neighbours. Any neighbour-averaged quantity converges to the global mean as this grows, so neighbour-relative views lose resolution on high-degree graphs.",
 "max_degree": "Largest neighbour count.",
 "degree_std": "Standard deviation of the degree.",
 "clustering_coeff": "Average local clustering coefficient (triangle closure). Estimated by sampling above 2M edges.",
 "num_communities": "Number of communities found by Louvain. Louvain is run WITHOUT a fixed seed, so this and the two fields below vary slightly between runs.",
 "modularity": "Modularity of that Louvain partition. Below ~0.3 the partition is weak, so community-relative views have little to measure against.",
 "homophily": "NOT label homophily and NOT feature homophily. It is the fraction of edges whose two endpoints fall in the SAME LOUVAIN COMMUNITY, computed from structure alone. It says nothing about whether neighbours have similar attributes.",
 "feature_dim": "Number of node attributes.",
 "feature_sparsity": "Fraction of attribute entries that are exactly zero.",
 "feature_dup_rate": "Fraction of nodes whose attribute row is byte-identical to at least one other node's row. High values mean template-dominated attributes.",
 "spectral_gap": "Second-smallest eigenvalue of the UNNORMALISED Laplacian (algebraic connectivity). It scales with degree, so it is comparable across graphs only at similar average degree.",
 "is_power_law": "Heuristic only: true when degree_std > 2 * avg_degree.",
 "how_to_read_the_landmarkers": "Each landmarker is the full score vector of one cheap paradigm, min-max normalised to [0,1] and then summarised. Normalisation is per paradigm, so the mean and the quantiles are comparable ACROSS paradigms only as shape, never as strength. A landmarker also cannot tell you the sign of the signal: a mechanism that is present but inverted on this graph produces the same shape as one that is present and correct."
}

messages.content: You are the analyst of an unsupervised graph anomaly detection framework. You are given a label-free profile of an attributed graph and the catalog of applicable detection paradigms, each with the assumption it relies on. You do not know how the graph was built or what its anomalies look like; reason only from the evidence given. Select the small set of paradigms (1 to 4) whose assumptions the evidence supports, favouring complementary views over redundant ones. Reply with JSON only.

HOW TO READ THE EVIDENCE (definitions of the fields below; read them literally, some names are narrower than they sound):
{
 "how_to_read_the_profile": "Each field is a label-free statistic of this graph. Read the definitions literally: several fields do not mean what their name suggests.",
 "num_nodes": "Number of nodes.",
 "num_edges": "Number of directed edge entries in the edge list (each undirected edge appears twice).",
 "density": "num_edges / (n*(n-1)). A value above ~0.01 means neighbourhoods cover a large share of the graph.",
 "avg_degree": "Mean number of neighbours. Any neighbour-averaged quantity converges to the global mean as this grows, so neighbour-relative views lose resolution on high-degree graphs.",
 "max_degree": "Largest neighbour count.",
 "degree_std": "Standard deviation of the degree.",
 "clustering_coeff": "Average local clustering coefficient (triangle closure). Estimated by sampling above 2M edges.",
 "num_communities": "Number of communities found by Louvain. Louvain is run WITHOUT a fixed seed, so this and the two fields below vary slightly between runs.",
 "modularity": "Modularity of that Louvain partition. Below ~0.3 the partition is weak, so community-relative views have little to measure against.",
 "homophily": "NOT label homophily and NOT feature homophily. It is the fraction of edges whose two endpoints fall in the SAME LOUVAIN COMMUNITY, computed from structure alone. It says nothing about whether neighbours have similar attributes.",
 "feature_dim": "Number of node attributes.",
 "feature_sparsity": "Fraction of attribute entries that are exactly zero.",
 "feature_dup_rate": "Fraction of nodes whose attribute row is byte-identical to at least one other node's row. High values mean template-dominated attributes.",
 "spectral_gap": "Second-smallest eigenvalue of the UNNORMALISED Laplacian (algebraic connectivity). It scales with degree, so it is comparable across graphs only at similar average degree.",
 "is_power_law": "Heuristic only: true when degree_std > 2 * avg_degree.",
 "how_to_read_the_landmarkers": "Each landmarker is the full score vector of one cheap paradigm, min-max normalised to [0,1] and then summarised. Normalisation is per paradigm, so the mean and the quantiles are comparable ACROSS paradigms only as shape, never as strength. A landmarker also cannot tell you the sign of the signal: a mechanism that is present but inverted on this graph produces the same shape as one that is present and correct."
}

GRAPH PROFILE (label-free):
{
 "num_nodes": 11758,
 "num_edges": 1038000,
 "density": 0.015017,
 "avg_degree": 88.28,
 "max_degree": 2138,
 "degree_std": 161.82,
 "clustering_coeff": 0.5329,
 "num_communities": 26,
 "modularity": 0.5194,
 "homophily": 0.7492,
 "feature_dim": 10,
 "feature_sparsity": 0.4803,
 "feature_dup_rate": 0.489,
 "spectral_gap": 0.132,
 "is_power_law": false
}

  "assumption": "Anomalous nodes are hard to reconstruct from their neighborhood",
  "computes": "A two-layer GCN autoencoder (GCN encoder to 64 dims, GCN decoder back to feature width) trained 100 epochs to minimise mean squared error on the node attributes; the score is the per-node reconstruction error.",

  "provenance": "Generic implementation of the paradigm, not a port of DOMINANT or AnomalyDAE, and not method-equivalent to them.",

  "inputs": "Node attributes. It does not read the edges at all.",
  "degenerates_when": "Attributes are high-dimensional or binary and sparse, where nearest-neighbour distances concentrate and the factor loses meaning.",
  "provenance": "Standard LOF applied to node attributes.",
  "applicable_because": "num_nodes = 11758 satisfies >= 30"
 },
 {
  "name": "community",
  "assumption": "Anomalous nodes don't fit any community well",
  "computes": "Assigns each node to a Louvain community, takes the centroid of the raw attributes of that community, and scores the node by its distance to that centroid divided by the community's mean distance.",
  "reference_frame": "Community-relative: each node is compared with its own community's attribute centroid.",
  "inputs": "Node attributes and the Louvain partition of the edges.",
  "degenerates_when": "Modularity is low or the communities are few and very large, because the centroid is then close to the global mean and the normalisation by the community spread removes what is left.",

  "applicable_because": "num_communities = 26 satisfies >= 2"

  "name": "homophily_violation",
  "assumption": "Anomalous nodes have features that mismatch their neighbors",
  "computes": "Averages the raw attribute rows of a node's neighbours and scores the node by the Euclidean distance between its own row and that average.",
  "reference_frame": "Neighbour-relative, on raw attributes and unnormalised, so it is sensitive to attribute scale.",
  "inputs": "Node attributes and edges. Nodes with no neighbours get the median score.",
  "degenerates_when": "Average degree is large, for the same reason as local affinity: the neighbour average converges to the global mean.   "provenance": "Ours.",
  "applicable_because": "homophily = 0.749 satisfies >= 0.4"
 },
 {
  "name": "spectral",
  "assumption": "Anomalous nodes produce high-frequency signals on the graph",
  "computes": "Reduces the attributes to a single scalar per node, the L2 norm of its attribute row, and measures the high-frequency energy of that scalar signal on the graph: the top half of the Laplacian eigenvectors below 3000 nodes, otherwise the residual of one-hop smoothing.",

  "applicable_because": "num_nodes = 11758 satisfies >= 30"
 },

  "computes": "Builds two rankings, one by mean distance to the 10 nearest neighbours in attribute space and one by the homophily-violation score, and scores each node by the absolute difference between its two ranks.",
  "reference_frame": "Cross-modal: it measures disagreement between an attribute-space view and a neighbour-relative view.",
